newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-FTSE to claw back losses, aiming for 4,620.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-FTSE to claw back losses, aiming for 4,620.

text.p: A firm start on the London stock market should see the FTSE 100 index climb up to around 4,620 on Wednesday, technical analysts said.

Market sentiment changed for the better on Tuesday, when the index turned a 37 point loss to a 20 point gain and this should be enough to allow the market to claw back a little more of the 186 points it has now lost since June 13, they added.
And as confidence returns, the banks, pharmaceuticals and oils sectors may once again find their form to take the index nudging upwards.
By 0713 GMT, the FTSE was indicated up 7.8 at 4,604.1.

Apart from bargain-hunting for stocks which appear to have been oversold, some institutional investors may indulge in a little window dressing as the second quarter of the financial year comes to an end, analysts said.
This is when investors sell underperforming stocks and buy those that are outperforming in order to boost their funds performance for over the quarter.
"But by its nature, window dressing is a short-lived phenomenon and share price volatility could return soon afterwards," one analyst said.
